claims.claim: Reviewers report that the base game lacks content after a short time and that mods are needed to reach its full potential or play with more than two players.

citations.review_text: I will 100% recommend this game but there is one thing stopping it from being perfect, and it's that there's nothing to do after playing the base game for 30 minutes. you basically need to mod this game for it to reach its peak, although i can safely say once you do that this game is absolutely hilarious with 4 people

One of my absolute favorite games. It makes for a great couch co-op game, and having a unique build each run keeps the game from feeling stale for me. It's fantastic that there is a modding community for this game; in fact, I don't play this game without mods, for better or worse. The mods that allow me to play with more than just a few players as well as the ones that allow you to continue after a win / loss make the game far more replayable in my opinion. Specifically allowing the players to keep playing really helps builds come to fruition. The criticisms that I have with the game is that some of these features feel like they could have been built-in, and that the game is buggy. I've always had trouble getting it to just play and keep playing-- but once you're up and running, there are very few games that can compete with how fun this is. Anyway. I love this game, and Landfall always makes stellar games. Support these devs!

Definitely a fun game, the only thing it's truly missing is 4-person. Which is possible with mods I think. Also the game is a tad buggy and the way it handles ping above 150ms means the game starts being unplayable.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe inconsistencies with blocking mechanics and client-side bullets during matches.

citations.review_text: Well rounded, blocking and client side bullets are not consistent.

An arcade fighting game in which each player evolves the abilities of their character on each loss.

[hr][/hr]
Rounds is a 2D shooter all about one-on-one duels. You and your opponent are thrown Ito a random stage and must kill each other, being rewarded half a point when you’re successful. Once a player earns a full point, they win the round, with the first to 5 rounds won taking the game.

Your characters can of course walk, jump, duck and shoot, depleting a limited pool of three bullets that is refilled after a few seconds. Shots have noticeable travel time and are affected by gravity, forcing you to predict where your opponent will move and which path your bullets will take. To make things more interesting, you can also block on a cooldown, with properly timed blocks cancelling any damage and reflecting shots that hit you. Beyond being shot, players will also take damage from touching the edges of the screen and when being hit by physics objects, giving you some additional tactical options.

The thing differentiating Rounds from any standard arcade shooter is the fact, that you can upgrade your character’s abilities, creating a build to counter your opponent. When a match starts, each player gets to pick a single upgrade, with another one being given to the losing player after each round, letting you stack up to 5 of them. When choosing an upgrade, you’re given 5 cards to pick from, each of which provides a different effect you get until the end of the match.

These card effects are mostly made up of basic number tweaks, like increasing your health or bullet speed, as well as minor bonus effects, like letting your blocks do damage, having bullets push your apply push forces or making your block freeze your opponent when nearby. Beyond these, there are also some rare cards with entirely unique abilities, like gaining a revive, shooting endlessly in exchange for health or directly controlling the movement of shot bullets.
